english.title: Handling fish in suspicious circumstances
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) at a time when you believed or it would have been reasonable for you to suspect that a relevant offence, namely **(..SPECIFY OFFENCE..), had been committed in relation to fish to which section 32 of the Salmon Act 1986 applied, namely **(..SPECIFY FISH..), received that fish, or undertook or assisted in its retention, removal or disposal or arranged to do so
english.legislation: Contrary to section 32 of the Salmon Act 1986.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 32(1A) of the Salmon Act 1986 specifies the type of fish in relation to which an offence is a relevant offence.

other.penalty:
Indictment: Fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Summary: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
NoneNote
Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
